problem: RL social-navigation policies are fast but lack semantic/social reasoning and generalize poorly to rare human interactions, while VLM-based navigators reason well but are too slow and costly for real-time use.
motivation: Semantic reasoning is unnecessary overhead in uncrowded navigation but becomes critical when a human is close. Invoking a VLM only in socially sensitive moments could give both real-time speed and social competence.
key_idea: Run a Falcon-style RL policy by default and hand control to a LoRA-post-trained small VLM (Qwen3-VL-2B) when a rolling personal-space-compliance (PSC) score drops below a threshold.
insight: Conditional triggering with a small fine-tuned VLM improves SR and human collisions over RL-only Falcon. The trigger threshold matters: r=0.80 m is best, while larger r causes many more VLM calls and worse SR (55.75 at 0.90 m, 3250 calls). Input representation matters too: depth JET colormap with Canny edges beats RGB and mixed inputs and is faster (2,425 ms/call vs 4,580 ms/call for RGB). The freeze-timing assumption is optimistic: realistic timing costs about 5 SR points (62.07→56.90).
method: RL navigation policy: Falcon's pretrained DD-PPO policy (depth encoder + point-goal + 2-layer LSTM) with social-cognition penalties (collision, proximity, trajectory obstruction) and auxiliary human count/position/trajectory losses; outputs discrete actions.

VLM reasoning module: Qwen3-VL-2B fine-tuned with SFT+LoRA (r=16, α=32, ~17M trainable params) that maps a fused image and prompt to the next n (8) discrete action tokens like [FORWARD]/[LEFT]/[STOP].

Visual token pre-processing: depth is normalized, JET-colormapped for distance zones, overlaid with Canny edge contours and the rendered goal vector into one fused image; goal distance/angle is also written into the text prompt.
PSC switch: PSC_W = fraction of the last W steps with human distance >1.0 m; use RL if PSC_W ≥ θ, else switch to the VLM (best trigger r=0.8).
VLM training data selection: SFT on the SNEI social-navigation VQA set, chosen over MUSON because it gives the best action accuracy (0.850).
Real-world deployment: ROS2 node on the Mirokaï robot using onboard depth camera plus OptiTrack for human positions, converting discrete actions to velocity commands.

setting.backbone: Falcon RL policy (DD-PPO, pretrained) + Qwen3-VL-2B (LoRA fine-tuned)
setting.model_size: 2.1B VLM (~17M trainable LoRA params) + small RL policy
setting.training_data: RL policy is pretrained Falcon; VLM is SFT'd on SNEI (SCAN-based social navigation VQA) image-question-answer pairs
setting.observation: egocentric depth (VLM also uses RGB in ablations) + relative point-goal + distance to closest human
setting.action_space: discrete high-level actions (forward, left, right, stop; VLM outputs 8-action plans)
setting.privileged: human positions/distances (GT in sim; OptiTrack motion capture in real world); simulator frozen during VLM inference in main results

numbers_note: Benchmark split names are not stated in the paper; 'val' is assumed. The ablation tables appear to be on Social-HM3D, since the Freeze row matches Table 1's HM3D result.
results: HUMA reaches SR 62.07 on Social-HM3D and 70.35 on Social-MP3D, beating NavThinker (59.46 and 47.33) and Falcon (56.26 and 51.67). H-Coll drops to 34.48 and 20.82 while SPL and PSC stay competitive. Realistic timing reduces HM3D SR to 56.90.
limitations: VLM latency (~2.4 s/call): the main results freeze the simulator during inference, and realistic timing costs ~5 SR points.
Reactive trigger with a fixed threshold (0.8 m) that ignores scene density, and the VLM often pads its plan with 'forward' steps.
Sim-to-real domain gap: the VLM was trained on real RGB and may hallucinate on Habitat frames; the real-world demo is qualitative and uses motion capture.
